title: Return to making albums for Norman Granz
summary: After Montreux in 1975, Granz commissioned several albums in 1976 with Gillespie, Terry, Basie and others.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: albums. What was the occasion? How did that come about?

Well, in 1975, Norman Granz asked me to go to Montreux, to the festival, and play with, you know, his segment of -- I think Norman Granz had a night, or a couple of nights, and I went and did one of his nights there during which he recorded that program; I think that's been released as the Montreux Festival.

Then after that, he asked me if I would make, you know, some albums for him. And I made one, I believe, in February of '76 and a few weeks later, I made one with ... Dizzy Gillespie and I and the rhythm section, and then a few weeks later, made another with Clark Terry, Count Basie, Lockjaw Davis ... oh, who else was on that one; I think Louie Bellson. But that's about 3 in about 3 months, and now I'm scheduled to make another one on the 23rd of this month, which is just about 10 days away.
So you suddenly have a new rush of album activity?
It's very welcome to your fans and to others who ought to become fans.
